WEST PAKISTAN CAPITAL GAINS TAX RULES, 1964
WEST PAKISTAN CAPITAL GAINS TAX RULES, 1964
[Gazette of West Pakistan, Extraordinary, 29th June 1964]
No. 1379/64/738-Tax/II.-In exercise of the powers conferred on him
by subsection (1) of section 20 of the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1963 (West
Pakistan Act No. IX of 1963), read with section 16 thereof, the Governor of
West Pakistan is pleased to make the following rules :------
l. Title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the West
Pakistan Capital Gains Tax Rules, 1964.
(2) They shall come into force at once and shall be deemed to have
taken effect on and from the first day of July 1963.
2. Definition.-In these rules unless the context otherwise
requires the following expression shall have the meanings hereby respectively
assigned to them that is to say-
(a) " Act " means the West Pakistan Finance Act, 1963
(West Pakistan Act IX of 1963);
(b) " assessee " means a person by whom capital gains
tax is payable under the Act, and includes any person in respect of whom any
proceeding under the Act has been taken for the determination of capital gain
tax payable by him ;
(c) " Board of Revenue " means the Board of Revenue,
West Pakistan ;
(d) " capital gains tax " or " tax " means the
capital gains tax, levied under section 16 of the Act ;
(e) " Commissioner " means Commissioner having
jurisdiction in the urban area in which is situated the immovable property
yielding profits or gains liable to tax ;
(,f) " Director, Excise and Taxation " means the
Director, Excise and Taxation incharge of a revenue division ;
(g) " Excise and Taxation Officer " means the Excise and
Taxation Officers having jurisdiction in the urban area in which is situated
the immovable property yielding profits or gains liable to tax ;
(h) " forms " mean a forms appended to these rules ;
(i) " return " means a return in a form and includes a
statement or communication on plain paper containing the same particulars as
are specified in the corresponding form.
3. Assessment.-Every assessee shall, within thirty days of the publication
of these rules or within fifteen days of the sale, exchange or transfer of
immovable property concerned whichever is later, submit to the Excise and
Taxation Officer a return in Form CGT-1.
4. If the assessee fails or neglects to submit the return under
rule 3, the Excise and Taxation Officer shall serve the assessee with a notice
in Form CGT-2 requiring him to submit the return within such period as may be
specified in the notice.
5. If the Excise and Taxation Officer is satisfied that the return
submitted under rule 3 or rule 4 as the case may be, is correct and complete,
he shall accept such return and assess the capital gains tax payable on the
basis thereof.
6. If in the opinion of the Excise and Taxation Officer a return
submitted under rule 3 or rule 4 is not correct or complete, or no return is
furnished in response to the notice referred to in rule 4, he shall serve the
assessee with a notice in Form CGT-3 requiring him to appear before him and
after giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard and examining such
evidence as he may produce, and after making such enquiries as may be deemed
necessary, assess to the best of his judgment the Capital Gains Tax payable by
him.
7. If an assessee has sold exchanged or transferred immovable
property for valuable consideration other than money he shall separately
specify in the return the details of the valuable consideration received and
its estimated value in terms of money. The Excise and Taxation Officer .shall
after such enquiries as he may deem necessary determine the value of the
consideration in terms of money and assess the tax accordingly.
8. Determination of actual cost and value of consideration.-If in
the opinion of the Excise and Taxation Officer, the actual cost of property, as
stated by the assessee is not correct and is to be determined in pursuance of
